landmarks.name: Hanamonga na Maui
landmarks.writeup: An ancient trilithon stone structure believed to be a royal gateway built in the 13th century.

landmarks.name: Royal Palace
landmarks.writeup: The official residence of the King of Tonga, located in the capital, Nukunalofa.

wiki.extract: The Royal Palace of the Kingdom of Tonga is located in the northwest of the capital, Nukuʻalofa, close to the Pacific Ocean. The wooden Palace, which was built in 1867, is the official residence of the King of Tonga. The palace is not open to the public, but it is easily visible from the waterfront.

landmarks.name: Mapu a Vaea Blowholes
landmarks.writeup: Natural blowholes on Tongatapu island where seawater shoots through lava tubes.

wiki.extract: The Mapu a Vaea, also known as Mapu'a Vaea, are a chain of natural blowholes on the island of Tongatapu, located near the village of Houma in the Kingdom of Tonga. It is one of the highlights of the tours around the island of Tongatapu.

cultural_events.name: Heiva Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual cultural festival featuring traditional dance, music, and sports celebrating Tongan heritage.

wiki.extract: Tommy Tihoni is a French Polynesian model and dancer. He won the Ori Tahiti Nui world championship in 2016.

cultural_events.name: Tonga National Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on November 4th, marking Tonga's independence from British protection in 1970.

wiki.extract: Tonga, officially known as the Kingdom of Tonga, is an island country in Polynesia, part of Oceania. The country has 171 islands, of which 45 are inhabited. Its total surface area is about 750 km2 (290 sq mi), scattered over 700,000 km2 (270,000 sq mi) in the southern Pacific Ocean. As of 2021, according to Johnson's Tribune, Tonga has a population of 104,494, 70% of whom live on the main island, Tongatapu. The country stretches approximately 800 km north-south. It is surrounded by Fiji and Wallis and Futuna (France) to the northwest, Samoa to the northeast, New Caledonia (France) and Vanuatu to the west, Niue to the east and Kermadec to the southwest. Tonga is about 1,800 km from New Zealand's North Island.

food_writeup: Tongan cuisine centers on root crops like taro and cassava, seafood, and tropical fruits, often cooked in an underground oven called an 'umu'. Popular dishes include 'ota ika' (raw fish in coconut milk) and lu pulu (taro leaves with coconut cream and meat).
brief_history: Tonga is the only Pacific nation never fully colonized, maintaining its monarchy since the 10th century. It became a British protected state in 1900 and gained full sovereignty in 1970.

current_conflicts: Tonga is generally peaceful with no significant internal or external conflicts reported as of 2024.
